_comment: ubuntnix snap lockfile (SPEC.md §4.3, §4.4; GitHub issue #60, milestone M3). Generated by bin/ubx-snap-resolve: Snap Store resolution of the declared snap set in snaps.packages.json -- see bin/ubx-snap-resolve's header for the full mechanism. Consumed by nix/snap.nix via builtins.fromJSON; see that file for fetch mechanics and tests/lib/validate-snap-lockfile.py for the schema this file is held to. `snap.sha256`/`assert.sha256` below were recomputed locally (python3's hashlib) from bytes actually fetched from the live Snap Store while authoring this file -- the Store's own self-reported metadata (its JSON API's own 'sha3-384' field, cross-checked and found to agree: b07bdb78e762c2e6020c75fafc92055b323a6f8da3ab42a3963da5ade386aba11f77e3c8f919b8aa23f3aa5c06c844f9) is corroborating evidence, not the trust root, mirroring archive.lock.json's own methodology. `assert.sha256`/`assert.url` pin specifically the snap-declaration assertion (api.snapcraft.io's `/v1/snaps/assertions/snap-declaration/16/<snap-id>`, confirmed independently re-fetchable) -- NOT the full snap-revision+account+account-key chain a real `snap ack` needs for a fully offline install; see bin/ubx-snap-resolve's `_ubx_snap_resolve_real` header and docs/snap.md for why that's a deliberate, tracked scope reduction rather than an oversight. Snaps are sorted by name for a stable diff and a byte-identical re-resolution given unchanged inputs. Every entry here already passed the verified-publisher policy (SPEC.md §4.5/§5) at resolve time; nix/snap.nix re-enforces the identical policy independently at eval time.
